Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). Given the voluntary nature of the latter, this Court agrees with Skold that he was not required to refer this dispute to mediation before bringing suit here against Inc.
20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. 12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). Under such rules and laws, we may temporarily suspend processing of a transaction for greater scrutiny or verification against the OFAC list of blocked parties, which may result in delayed settlement, posting and/or availability of funds. If we determine there is a violation, or if we cannot satisfactorily resolve a suspected or potential violation, the subject funds will be blocked as required by law. If you believe you have adequate grounds to seek the return of any blocked funds, it is your sole responsibility to pursue the matter with the appropriate governmental authorities. Please see the OFAC website for procedures and form required to seek a release of blocked funds.

18	The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:

18	The more significant problem with Love-joy’s argument that it had an “unfettered” right to redefine the House Accounts is that this interpretation would nullify portions of the Agreement’s termination provision. PL’s Opp. Br. at 17. Under the termination provision, the Agreement became effective January 1, 2004, and:
19	shall continue in force for a one (1) year period, and shall be automatically renewed for additional one (1) year periods thereafter unless terminated by written notice from either party to the other party not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the initial or any subsequent one (1) year term.

The Agreement also provides for termination by either party under certain additional circumstances, including (1) a change of 50% or more of the ownership of the other party; (2) the other party’s unreasonable and repeated failure to perform the terms and conditions of the Agreement; or (3) the other party’s filing of a bankruptcy petition. 21	The termination provision, on its face, provides a comprehensive account of the ways in which the Agreement may be terminated. There is no indication in the Agreement that the parties contemplated that the House Accounts provision would constitute an additional means for terminating all of Lovejoy’s obligations under the Agreement. Under Lovejoy’s construction of the House Accounts provision, however, Lovejoy could, at any time and without Kamco’s consent, redefine every single account in Kamco’s territory as a House Account. This interpretation would allow Lovejoy to escape from all of its obligations under the Agreement and all of the restrictions in the termination provision.
22	This reading is inconsistent with Pennsylvania law, which, as noted above, forbids courts from “interpreting] one provision of a contract in a manner which results in another portion being annulled,” LJL Transp., 962 A.2d at 648 (citation omitted), and requires that “[t]he whole instrument ... be taken together in arriving at contractual intent,” Duquesne Univ., 777 A.2d at 429 (citation omitted). In other words, the “mutual” termination provision would never apply to Lovejoy.

Id. The evident purpose of this provision is to permit both parties to make business plans in reliance on the contract’s continued existence for a one year period. This purpose would obviously be frustrated if one party maintained a unilateral right to opt out of all of its obligations under the contract at any time — which is precisely how Lovejoy construes the House Accounts provision.
24	This court’s conclusion that Lovejoy’s reading of the House Accounts provision is inconsistent with the parties’ intent is reinforced by the fact that the Agreement contains a non-compete provision. The noncompetition provision states that Kamco could not, without Lovejoy’s permission, sell any product which is directly competitive with any Lovejoy product that Kamco was supposed to sell on Lovejoy’s behalf. Id. ¶ 2. If, as Lovejoy suggests, the House Accounts provision granted Lovejoy the “unfettered” right to redefine all or substantially all accounts as House Accounts, then Lovejoy would have the unilateral power to deprive Kamco of all of the benefits it was to receive under the contract while simultaneously barring Kamco from selling any product made by a Lovejoy competitor. Good faith duties are implied “where it is clear that an obligation is within the contemplation of the parties at the time of contracting or is necessary to carry out their intentions.” Slater v. Pearle Vision Center, Inc., 376 Pa.Super. 580, 546 A.2d 676, 679 (1988); see also Duquesne Light, 66 F.3d at 617 (noting that “courts generally utilize the good faith duty as an interpretive tool to determine the parties’ justifiable expectations”). Reading the House Accounts provision in this manner allows the termination provision to have its intended effect: If one of the parties wishes to put an end to its obligations to the other party, it must follow one of the enumerated ways of terminating the Agreement.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"A standard integration and precedence clause; the only soft edge is the phrase 'inconsistent with this Agreement', which is a familiar and workable formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Its precedence rule ('this Agreement shall govern') sits against Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1, which resolves inconsistencies by requiring the better quality/greater quantity as the Architect interprets, and against the Addendum's revisions, so a court could have to reconcile two different conflict-resolution regimes.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite; 'except to the extent specifically indicated' is anchored to the Contract Documents themselves.","reasoning_cat2":"The First Addendum expressly replaces Article 2 with a revised version, so the original is superseded rather than in conflict.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"The inserted date is 'Approximately the Fifteenth of July', and an approximate commencement date is inherently imprecise for measuring the Contract Time.","reasoning_cat2":"The First Addendum 4.1 fixes commencement at July 15, 2002 'pending approval of permits', which both supersedes and further conditions this clause, and 4.2 measures the Contract Time from the same date.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence, no undefined or elastic terms.","reasoning_cat2":"It depends on the commencement date in 4.1/Addendum 4.1 but does not contradict them.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"The number of calendar days is garbled and partially blank in the text, leaving the completion deadline unreadable on the face of the clause.","reasoning_cat2":"The First Addendum 4.3 substitutes a fixed date of November 30, 2003, so the two must be read together and the original day-count is displaced.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"The 'Contract Sum' is defined as Cost of the Work plus Fee, but whether that sum is capped, and what 'Cost of the Work' captures given Article 7's closed list and Article 8's exclusions, is exactly the kind of payment-basis definition parties read differently.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be squared with 5.2.1, where the guaranteed maximum figure is left blank/'N/A', and with 8.1.8, 12.1.5 and 12.1.7.1, all of which compute payment by reference to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that may not exist; that is a genuine whole-instrument tension.","prob_cat1":0.46,"prob_cat2":0.71},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"The Fee is stated as a flat $380,000 with none of the bracketed method for adjusting the Fee for changes filled in, leaving a lump-sum fee with no stated adjustment mechanism.","reasoning_cat2":"Paragraph 6.4 and 12.1.7.3 both contemplate either a rate or a fixed sum and supply fallback machinery, and Addendum 8.1.8 says the Fee covers listed overhead, so the clause interacts with several provisions without squarely contradicting them.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"The operative guarantee reads 'not to exceed N/A Dollars ($ N/A)', so the central number of a guaranteed-maximum-price contract is missing; whether a cap exists at all turns on that entry.","reasoning_cat2":"8.1.8, 12.1.5, 12.1.6, 12.1.7.1, 13.2 and Addendum 6.5 all operate by allocating or policing a Guaranteed Maximum Price, and none of them can function if the figure is 'N/A' — a direct whole-instrument incoherence.","prob_cat1":0.61,"prob_cat2":0.74},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"A blank fill-in for alternates with only boilerplate instruction text; nothing operative to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"It presupposes a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves blank, but the blank alternates list adds nothing of its own.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"A blank heading for unit prices with no content.","reasoning_cat2":"Nothing elsewhere depends on unit prices, and no conflicting provision appears.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"A blank heading for allowances with only bracketed instructions.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision allocates allowances, so the blank creates no inconsistency.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"The assumptions underpinning the GMP are left blank, which is an absence rather than an ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"Because 5.2.1 leaves the GMP itself blank and 5.2.6 speaks of development 'reasonably inferable', the absence of stated assumptions could matter to reconciling those provisions.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonably inferable therefrom' and the exclusion of 'changes in scope, systems, kinds and quality of materials' draw a line that parties routinely dispute.","reasoning_cat2":"It assumes a priced GMP that 5.2.1 leaves blank and overlaps with Addendum 6.5's fast-track development procedure, which routes increased costs into the Cost of the Work by Change Order.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"A short permissive cross-reference to A201 §7.3.3 methods; nothing elastic.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.2, 6.3 and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1's change-order requirement.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"Long but precise definitional mapping of 'cost' and 'fee' to A201 usage, with a stated carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"It coordinates with 6.3 and Article 7 and expressly says it shall not be modified by Articles 5, 7 and 8, which reduces rather than creates tension.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"It defines the Contractor's Fee by reference to 'Subparagraph 5.1.1', but the Fee is actually stated in 5.1.2 — a cross-reference error on the face of the clause.","reasoning_cat2":"The mis-citation must be corrected by reading 5.1.1 and 5.1.2 together, and 13.4 makes the same mapping using 5.1.2, exposing the inconsistency.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c017","reasoning_cat1":"'Substantial inequity' and 'equitably adjusted' are open-textured standards with no metric supplied.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to adjustment provisions 'in Paragraph 5.1' that were largely left blank, and it presupposes a GMP that 5.2.1 does not supply.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c018","reasoning_cat1":"'Costs necessarily incurred ... in the proper performance of the Work' and 'rates not higher than the standard paid at the place of the Project' are both judgment-laden phrases, and the closing sentence limits recovery to the enumerated Article 7 items.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit A and Exhibit C set contractor-owned equipment and hand-tool rates, and Addendum 8.1.8 removes several categories from reimbursement, so the boundary of the Cost of the Work is set in more than one place.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c019","reasoning_cat1":"A concrete category of wages tied to direct employment and site location.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Exhibit B's labor rate sheet and with 8.1.1's exclusion of principal-office personnel.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c020","reasoning_cat1":"Reimbursement turns on personnel being 'stationed at the site with the Owner's approval', a condition whose satisfaction is factual rather than textually ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"8.1.1 excludes principal-office personnel 'except as specifically provided in 7.2.2 and 7.2.3', and Addendum 8.1.8 says the Fee covers senior management and administrative support, which narrows this item.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c021","reasoning_cat1":"Limited to the portion of time required for the Work; the categories are specific.","reasoning_cat2":"It is expressly preserved by 8.1.1's carve-out but potentially cut back by Addendum 8.1.8's fee-covers-management list.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c022","reasoning_cat1":"The internal cross-reference ('Subparagraphs 7.1.1 through 7.2.j') is garbled, and 'customary benefits' is an open category illustrated by examples.","reasoning_cat2":"It depends on 7.2.1-7.2.3 remaining reimbursable, which Addendum 8.1.8 partly qualifies, but no direct contradiction appears.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c023","reasoning_cat1":"A plain cost category with transportation and storage expressly included.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits with 7.4.2, 7.5.6 and 12.1.7.2 on stored materials without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c024","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable waste and spoilage' is a soft measure but is a familiar trade standard.","reasoning_cat2":"It coordinates with 9.1-9.2 on credits accruing to the Owner without contradicting them.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c025","reasoning_cat1":"'Hand tools not customarily owned by construction workers' and 'fully consumed' are elastic tests, and cost for previously used items is set at 'fair market value' without a method.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit C says the cost of all such hand tools shall be borne by the Contractor and substitutes a flat 5% payroll add-on, which pulls against this clause's direct-cost reimbursement.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c026","reasoning_cat1":"Rental charges are bounded by the Owner's prior approval of rates and quantities; the wording is workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit A fixes equipment rates and Exhibit C states rates for equipment not owned by Contractor are at invoiced cost, while 8.1.5 excludes rental costs except as provided here, so three documents must be harmonised.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c027","reasoning_cat1":"A single, concrete cost item.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision addresses debris removal costs differently.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c028","reasoning_cat1":"A specific enumerated list closed by 'reasonable petty cash expenses of the site office'.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 8.1.8 states the Fee covers all main-office telephone, postage, supplies, facsimiles and stationery and that none of those items are directly reimbursable under Article 7, creating a boundary dispute with this clause.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c029","reasoning_cat1":"'That portion of the reasonable expenses ... incurred while travelling in discharge of duties connected with the Work' is loose but conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 8.1.8's list of fee-covered items and 8.1.2's exclusion of principal-office expenses both bear on which travel is reimbursable.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c030","reasoning_cat1":"Conditioned on advance Owner approval and a mutually acceptable location; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches 12.1.7.2's treatment of off-site stored materials.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c031","reasoning_cat1":"'That portion ... that can be directly attributed to this Contract' requires an allocation judgment but names the test.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit D fixes the general liability premium at 1% of labour and subcontractor costs, a formula that may not equal the portion 'directly attributable', so the two must be reconciled.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c032","reasoning_cat1":"'Sales, use or similar taxes ... related to the Work' uses a general catch-all after two specifics, though in a familiar tax formulation.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit D prescribes how Hawaii general excise tax is computed and exempts subcontract costs, which is a more detailed and potentially different rule than this clause.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c033","reasoning_cat1":"Tied to permits the Contractor is required by the Contract Documents to pay for; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with A201's permit obligations; no competing provision found.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c034","reasoning_cat1":"Precise, with two express carve-outs by cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"The cross-references to A201 13.5.3 and to 7.7.3 are consistent with those provisions as revised by the Addendum.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c035","reasoning_cat1":"Dense but specific; the sentence excluding defense costs from the Fee calculation 'or subject to the Guaranteed Maximum Price' is the only awkward passage.","reasoning_cat2":"It presupposes an operative GMP that 5.2.1 leaves blank and cross-refers to A201 3.17.1, but nothing squarely contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c036","reasoning_cat1":"'Data processing costs related to the Work' is broad and undefined, though a small-dollar category.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 8.1.8's list of fee-covered office and accounting expenses may swallow part of it.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c037","reasoning_cat1":"Turns on 'negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility', a phrase used consistently elsewhere in Article 7 and 8.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallels 7.7.3 and 8.1.6, which use the same formulation, so the instrument is internally consistent here.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c038","reasoning_cat1":"Clear carve-out for Owner-Contractor disputes and an express reasonableness qualifier on approval.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with A201's dispute provisions and with 8.1.7's residual exclusion.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c039","reasoning_cat1":"Keyed to the Contractor's own 'standard personnel policy', a document not part of the Contract Documents, which leaves the measure outside the instrument.","reasoning_cat2":"8.1.1 and Addendum 8.1.8 exclude principal-office compensation and overhead, which may cut across relocation allowances for such personnel.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c040","reasoning_cat1":"A pure catch-all ('Other costs incurred in the performance of the Work') but expressly gated by advance written Owner approval.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits alongside 8.1.7, which excludes any cost 'not specifically and expressly described in Article 7', and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1, which allows change only by Change Order, so the reach of this catch-all can be contested.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c041","reasoning_cat1":"Concrete emergency category cross-referenced to A201 10.6.","reasoning_cat2":"The First Addendum expressly revises 7.7.2 to add two limitations, so the unrevised text must be read as displaced.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c042","reasoning_cat1":"Conditioned on absence of negligence and non-recoverability from insurance and others; workable though fact-intensive.","reasoning_cat2":"The First Addendum revises 7.7.3 to add an insurance-maintenance proviso, so the two versions coexist in the document and must be reconciled.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c043","reasoning_cat1":"A bare introductory line to the exclusions list.","reasoning_cat2":"Serves as the chapeau for 8.1.1-8.1.8, which the Addendum partly rewrites, but the chapeau itself is neutral.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c044","reasoning_cat1":"The exception 'or as may be provided in Article 14' is open-ended, and Article 14 of the Agreement contains no such provision.","reasoning_cat2":"It cross-refers to 7.2.2 and 7.2.3, and Addendum 8.1.8 adds a further fee-covers-management rule, so the scope of excluded home-office compensation is set in three places.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c045","reasoning_cat1":"A short, categorical exclusion.","reasoning_cat2":"Overlaps with Addendum 8.1.8's expanded list of fee-covered office expenses but points the same way.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c046","reasoning_cat1":"'Overhead and general expenses' is an accounting term of art whose boundary against Article 7's site costs is notoriously contestable.","reasoning_cat2":"The exception 'except as may be expressly included in Article 7' plus Addendum 8.1.8's enumeration of fee-covered overhead means two provisions define the same boundary differently.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c047","reasoning_cat1":"A narrow exclusion with a single express cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit A's rate sheet and Exhibit C's rental provisions supply rates for Contractor-owned equipment, which must be squared with this exclusion and 7.5.2.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c048","reasoning_cat1":"Broad but standard fault-based exclusion with an express carve-out for 7.7.3.","reasoning_cat2":"The Addendum's revision of 7.7.3 changes the carve-out's content, so the exclusion's practical reach shifts with it.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c049","reasoning_cat1":"A pure expressio unius residual exclusion — 'any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7' — that squarely confronts Article 7's open items such as 7.7.1.","reasoning_cat2":"Read against 7.7.1's 'other costs approved in advance in writing' and Exhibits A-D, which add cost categories not spelled out in Article 7, the exclusion is hard to apply literally.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c050","reasoning_cat1":"The exclusion depends entirely on a Guaranteed Maximum Price figure, and its own wording gives no content if none exists.","reasoning_cat2":"5.2.1 leaves the GMP as 'N/A' and the First Addendum replaces 8.1.8 with an entirely different fee-covers-overhead provision, so this exclusion appears both unsupported and superseded.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.56},
{"clause_id":"c051","reasoning_cat1":"A two-limb rule for cash discounts with a clear 'otherwise' fallback, plus a specific list for trade discounts and rebates.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 9.1.1 adds a seven-day notice and funding right that qualifies when the Contractor may keep discounts, so the two operate together.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c052","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line accounting direction.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.1 and with 7.4.2's crediting mechanism.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c053","reasoning_cat1":"'Portions of the Work that the Contractor does not customarily perform with its own personnel' and 'reasonable objection' are both elastic tests.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 6.5 sets its own bidding procedure (at least two bids, Owner-named subcontractors reasonably acceptable to Contractor), which overlaps and partly differs from this bid-delivery regime.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c054","reasoning_cat1":"A precise three-condition test with a defined measure of adjustment.","reasoning_cat2":"The remedy is an adjustment to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves blank, and Addendum 6.5 provides a different Change Order mechanism keyed to the Contract Sum.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c055","reasoning_cat1":"A simple period definition with an unfilled 'or as follows' alternative.","reasoning_cat2":"Works with 12.1.3's application deadlines and Addendum 12.1.4's added submittals without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.10}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c104","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (ii) — costs 'capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition' — is an open counterfactual test with no standard of timeliness.","reasoning_cat2":"It is a revision of Agreement 7.7.2, whose unrevised text also appears in the instrument, so the two versions must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c105","reasoning_cat1":"Adds a proviso about absence of collectible insurance; the terms are specific though layered.","reasoning_cat2":"It revises Agreement 7.7.3, which appears unrevised elsewhere, and depends on insurance requirements that Article 16 leaves blank.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c106","reasoning_cat1":"A long enumerated list of fee-covered items closing with 'estimating/project purchasing costs and expenses', and the sweeping 'none of these items shall be subject to direct reimbursement under Article 7' invites an ejusdem generis fight over its edges.","reasoning_cat2":"It carries the number of the Agreement's 8.1.8 (costs exceeding the Guaranteed Maximum Price) while saying something entirely different, and it contradicts 7.5.4's reimbursement of telephone, postage and facsimile costs and 7.6.6's data processing costs.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c107","reasoning_cat1":"A clear notice-and-opportunity mechanism with a stated period.","reasoning_cat2":"It supplements Agreement 9.1's default rule that cash discounts otherwise accrue to the Contractor, narrowing but not contradicting it.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c108","reasoning_cat1":"'All in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' is a subjective standard with no reasonableness qualifier in the chapeau.","reasoning_cat2":"It bears the same number as the Agreement's own 12.1.4, which imposes a different set of substantiation requirements, so two provisions share one designation.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c109","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed itemisation of what the statement must show; concrete.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 12.1.7 and with 9.6.2.1's joint-payment mechanism.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c110","reasoning_cat1":"It requires lien waivers 'establishing payment or satisfaction' for amounts included in the current application without saying whether the waivers are conditional or unconditional — a recurring source of argument.","reasoning_cat2":"It ties into Addendum 12.2.2's lien-free title endorsement condition and 12.2.1's Notice of Completion, which are consistent in direction.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c111","reasoning_cat1":"A pure catch-all — 'such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require' — following two specific items, which is the classic general-after-specific structure.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels the Agreement's 12.1.4 catch-all and creates no separate inconsistency.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c112","reasoning_cat1":"The retainage is fixed at five percent and the fee computation covers both rate and fixed-sum cases; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It replaces the Agreement's 12.1.7.3, which states retainage as 'N/A percent', so the document contains two versions of the same subparagraph with different numbers.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c113","reasoning_cat1":"A single objective condition tied to publication and recordation.","reasoning_cat2":"It adds a third condition to 12.2.1 and dovetails with Addendum 12.2.2's recordation-based deadline, but sits against 12.2.3's Architect-certificate sequence.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c114","reasoning_cat1":"'Whichever is earlier' compares a recordation date with a lien-free endorsement date, either of which may never occur, leaving the trigger for final payment uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement's 12.2.2 fixes final payment at 30 days after the Architect's final Certificate, and 12.2.3 builds a certificate-based sequence, so two different final-payment triggers coexist.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c115","reasoning_cat1":"Naming 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' leaves three alternative representatives without saying who binds the Owner.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 says the Owner's authorized representative 'is Mary Williamson' while listing three people who may act, so the identity of the representative is stated three different ways.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c116","reasoning_cat1":"A chapeau reciting survival and materiality; standard.","reasoning_cat2":"It fills the Agreement's blank 14.6 and adds to representations elsewhere, without contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c117","reasoning_cat1":"'Financially solvent' and 'sufficient working capital' are judgment terms, but the representation is a factual warranty rather than a scope term.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision addresses Contractor solvency; A201 2.2.1 imposes the mirror obligation on the Owner.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c118","reasoning_cat1":"'Sufficient experience and competence' is a soft measure inside an otherwise plain capability warranty.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Addendum Article 2's skilled-staff requirement.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c119","reasoning_cat1":"'All necessary governmental and public and quasi-public authorities' is broad, but licensing status is an objective fact.","reasoning_cat2":"No competing licensing provision appears in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c120","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional site-visit representation with defined content.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates A201 1.5.2's execution representation, an overlap that points the same way.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c121","reasoning_cat1":"Self-identifying and precise.","reasoning_cat2":"It supersedes the Agreement's 15.1.1 and is consistent with Article 1's enumeration requirement.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c122","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies the edition and the modifying document plainly.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement's own 15.1.2 describes 'the 1991 edition' of A201-1997, so this revision is needed to cure a mismatch in the enumeration.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c123","reasoning_cat1":"Incorporation of 'Articles 1 through 14 inclusive' is a bounded and definite reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement Article 1 provides that the Agreement governs any inconsistency with other Contract Documents, so the scope of this wholesale incorporation must be read against that precedence rule.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c124","reasoning_cat1":"'Modify, change, delete from, and add to' followed by a survival rule for unaltered provisions is workable but requires judgment about what counts as altered.","reasoning_cat2":"It creates a third layer of precedence alongside Agreement Article 1 and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1, and several supplements duplicate rather than cleanly replace Agreement provisions.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c125","reasoning_cat1":"'Wherever in the Contract Documents a matter requires notice to ... the Architect' sweeps across the whole instrument, and the disclaimer of responsibility 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner' is broadly drawn.","reasoning_cat2":"It grafts an Owner consent requirement onto every Architect function in A201, including certification under 9.4 and initial decisions under 4.4, which sits awkwardly with the Architect's independent role in those provisions.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c126","reasoning_cat1":"'Better quality or greater quantity', 'more stringent requirement' and 'either or both' give no rule for choosing between the two limbs and are inherently comparative.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement Article 1 says that where the other Contract Documents are inconsistent with the Agreement, the Agreement governs; this clause instead resolves all inconsistencies in favour of more work as the Architect interprets — two different conflict rules in one instrument.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.52},
{"clause_id":"c127","reasoning_cat1":"A precise drawing-precedence rule.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 1.2.1.1's general scheme; no Drawings are enumerated, but that bears on 15.1.5 rather than here.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c128","reasoning_cat1":"The flat bar on 'extra charge or compensation ... on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated on the Drawings' is absolute and one-sided in drafting.","reasoning_cat2":"It pulls against A201 3.2 and 4.3.7 claim rights and against the change-order pricing machinery in Addendum 6.5, which contemplates payment for refinements as the design develops.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c129","reasoning_cat1":"'Minor change' is undefined here and 'sufficiently detailed drawings' supplies no standard.","reasoning_cat2":"A201 7.4 gives the Architect authority to order minor changes without cost or time effect, while Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 says changes may only be by Change Order, so three provisions govern the same ground.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c130","reasoning_cat1":"The first sentence names a single authorized representative and the next names three people who may act, an internal tension in two adjoining sentences.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 14.3 and Addendum 14.3 give two further formulations of who the Owner's representative is, and 14.5 requires notice before any change.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.39},
{"clause_id":"c131","reasoning_cat1":"A single seven-day cure period with a defined deduction remedy; clear enough on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"A201 2.4.1, reproduced in this instrument, requires a second seven-day notice before the Owner may act, so the revised and unrevised versions state different cure procedures.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c132","reasoning_cat1":"'Detailed timetable of all activities and events' and the deeming of the Schedule into the Contract Documents 'as it is developed' leave the Schedule's contractual force uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"A201 1.1.2 says the Contract may be amended only by Modification and Agreement Article 1 keys the Contract Documents to the Article 15 enumeration, yet this clause admits a document created later without either step.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c133","reasoning_cat1":"'Following completion of pre-construction services' and the three named design phases fix a sequence, but the clause makes every cost estimate 'part of the Contract Documents' without saying what contractual effect the estimate has.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 6.5 sets up a different pre-construction pricing regime (Preliminary Budget, Itemized Schedule of Values, Change Orders), and A201 1.1.2 permits amendment only by Modification, so three provisions describe how prices become binding.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c134","reasoning_cat1":"A specific submission and warranty requirement with an identifiable trigger.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with A201 3.12 and with Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's Owner-consent overlay.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c135","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed pleading requirement for time claims; concrete.","reasoning_cat2":"It supplements A201 4.3.7 without displacing its notice periods.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c136","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence is garbled and the notion of delays with 'concurrent or interrelated effects' is left undefined, so what is barred is unclear.","reasoning_cat2":"It qualifies A201 4.3.7 and 8.3.1 extensions of time; the direction is consistent even if the wording is loose.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c137","reasoning_cat1":"It bars any claim based on 'course of conduct or dealings', 'express or implied acceptance of alterations or additions' and unjust enrichment, subject only to two cross-referenced exceptions — a sweeping, one-sided exclusion whose reach against extra-work claims is exactly what parties fight over.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be reconciled with the cost-reimbursement structure of Articles 5 and 7, with Addendum 6.5's fast-track procedure in which prices are refined and Change Orders issued after the Work is under way, and with Supplementary Condition 3.10.5's later cost estimates that 'become part of the Contract Documents'.","prob_cat1":0.50,"prob_cat2":0.68},
{"clause_id":"c138","reasoning_cat1":"'Final settlement of all matters relating to the change ... including, but not limited to' combines an accord with an open-ended list.","reasoning_cat2":"It reinforces 7.1.3.1's change-order-only rule but sits against 6.4's equitable fee adjustment and the Addendum's iterative pricing.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c139","reasoning_cat1":"'Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary' and 'in their sole discretion' are strong but definite; the three no-privity disclaimers are precise.","reasoning_cat2":"It overrides other payment provisions by its own terms, which is a coordinated rather than conflicting drafting choice.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c140","reasoning_cat1":"'Received and accepted by the Owner' gives the Owner an unqualified acceptance right over final certification, without a reasonableness standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.1 and 12.2.3 make the final Certificate turn on the Architect's judgment and the accountants' report, so this adds an Owner veto to that sequence.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c141","reasoning_cat1":"A clear exclusion coupled with a waiver-of-subrogation requirement by cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement Article 16 leaves insurance limits blank, so the required policies to which this refers are not specified anywhere.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c142","reasoning_cat1":"'All reasonable costs ... properly attributable thereto' is a familiar and bounded formula.","reasoning_cat2":"It depends on 'insurance required under Article 11' at a time when Agreement Article 16 states no limits, leaving the required coverage undefined.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c143","reasoning_cat1":"It is headed 'construction costs to be reimbursed include' and then says the cost of hand tools 'shall be borne by the Contractor' before adding a 5% payroll surcharge, and the tool list is expressly non-exhaustive ('include, but are not limited to ... etc.') — both a self-contradiction and an open list.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.5.1 makes such hand tools a direct reimbursable cost and 8.1.5 excludes rental costs except under 7.5.2, so the flat percentage substitute cannot be squared with Article 7's itemised scheme.","prob_cat1":0.37,"prob_cat2":0.45},
{"clause_id":"c144","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed 1% formula applied to labour and subcontractor costs; arithmetically definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.6.1 reimburses only 'that portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract', which a flat percentage may exceed or fall short of.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c145","reasoning_cat1":"'All direct costs' is undefined and the list of vendor costs treated as 'Subcontract' costs is expressly open-ended ('including; rubbish hauling ... etc.'), so the exempt category has no fixed boundary.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.6.2 reimburses taxes 'related to the Work' without this carve-out, so the two set the tax base differently.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c146","reasoning_cat1":"A standard definitional list closed by an express exclusion of unenumerated bidding documents.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement Article 1 gives a slightly different list and a precedence rule, and Article 15's enumeration leaves Drawings and Specifications blank, so what is actually a Contract Document is contestable.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c147","reasoning_cat1":"Clear integration and no-privity language.","reasoning_cat2":"Its rule that the Contract 'may be amended or modified only by Modification' is hard to square with Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5, which make later schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents automatically.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c148","reasoning_cat1":"A broad but standard definition of the Work tied to the Contract Documents.","reasoning_cat2":"Because the Drawings and Specifications are not enumerated, the definition's referent is thin, but the definition itself is consistent throughout.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c149","reasoning_cat1":"A short definitional provision.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Agreement's identification of the Project.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c150","reasoning_cat1":"A descriptive definition with an illustrative list.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 15.1.5 enumerates no Drawings and dates them 'N/A', so the defined term has no identified content in this instrument.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c151","reasoning_cat1":"A descriptive definition of written requirements.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 15.1.4 lists no Specifications and refers to a Project Manual whose date is blank.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c152","reasoning_cat1":"'May include' makes the definition permissive but that is deliberate.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 15.1.3 and 15.1.4 refer to a Project Manual that is not dated or identified, so the definition has no referent here.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c153","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonably inferable from them as being necessary to produce the indicated results' is the classic scope phrase that construction parties read differently.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 resolves inconsistencies in favour of greater quantity while Agreement Article 1 gives the Agreement precedence, and Agreement 5.2.6 prices only development 'reasonably inferable' — three overlapping scope rules.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c154","reasoning_cat1":"A short and definite disclaimer about specification organisation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Agreement Article 10's subcontracting scheme.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c155","reasoning_cat1":"It imports 'well-known technical or construction industry meanings' without identifying them, which is a rule about meaning rather than a determinate term.","reasoning_cat2":"It supports rather than conflicts with the definitions in 1.1 and the Exhibits' trade terminology.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c156","reasoning_cat1":"A mechanical capitalisation convention.","reasoning_cat2":"No provision turns on it in a contested way.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c157","reasoning_cat1":"The provision is itself about omitted modifiers such as 'all' and 'any', so it acknowledges but does not itself create indeterminacy.","reasoning_cat2":"It is an interpretive aid consistent with the rest of Article 1.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c158","reasoning_cat1":"Two short sentences with a simple fallback of Architect identification.","reasoning_cat2":"Many of the Contract Documents here — Exhibits, the schedules deemed attached under 3.10.4 — are unsigned, so the identification mechanism carries weight but does not conflict.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c159","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional deemed representation on execution.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 14.6(d) contains a near-identical site-visit representation, an overlap in the same direction.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c160","reasoning_cat1":"Long but specific allocation of copyright and permitted uses, with express carve-outs.","reasoning_cat2":"No competing intellectual property provision appears; 7.6.5 addresses royalties separately and consistently.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c161","reasoning_cat1":"The transcription is badly broken, so the sentence about furnishing record legal title within fifteen days cannot be read continuously as printed.","reasoning_cat2":"It relates to Agreement 4.1's provision for Owner time to file mortgages and mechanic's lien notices, which was left blank, but nothing contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c162","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made' is an undefined standard and the clause makes it a 'condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work', which is strong medicine on soft wording.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against Article 12's payment machinery and Addendum 6.5's Owner termination right, but no provision squarely contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c163","reasoning_cat1":"A clear allocation with an express carve-out for permits under 3.7.1.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees a reimbursable Cost of the Work, which is consistent with the Contractor bearing them in the first instance.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c164","reasoning_cat1":"Reliance on Owner-furnished survey information subject to exercising 'proper precautions' is a familiar balanced formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for verifying measurements at the site, which cuts against reliance on Owner-furnished data.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c165","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable promptness' and 'any other information or services relevant to the Contractor's performance' are open but conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement Article 3 obliges the Owner to furnish and approve information in a timely manner, pointing the same way.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c166","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonably necessary' copies free of charge; a small, bounded obligation.","reasoning_cat2":"No Project Manual or Drawings are identified in Article 15, which thins the obligation but does not contradict it.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c167","reasoning_cat1":"'Persistently fails' is elastic, though the remedy and its limits are spelled out.","reasoning_cat2":"It coordinates with 2.4.1 and with Supplementary Condition 2.4.1's shortened cure procedure without contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.20},

{"clause_id":"c113","reasoning_cat1":"A single objective condition tied to publication and recordation.","reasoning_cat2":"It adds a third condition to 12.2.1 and dovetails with Addendum 12.2.2's recordation-based deadline, but sits against 12.2.3's Architect-certificate sequence.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.30},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c170","reasoning_cat1":"A single truncated sentence stating the core performance obligation; nothing elastic.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Agreement Article 2 and its revised Addendum counterpart.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c171","reasoning_cat1":"A clear non-waiver rule tied to specified categories of activity.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.2.3 and with Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's disclaimer of Owner responsibility.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c172","reasoning_cat1":"It imposes a study-and-compare duty while disclaiming that the duty is 'for the purpose of discovering errors', a tension that is well known but expressly addressed in the text.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for verifying measurements and bars extra charges, which hardens this obligation beyond what 3.2.1 says.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c173","reasoning_cat1":"'In the Contractor's capacity as a contractor and not as a licensed design professional' draws a clear line, though the reporting duty is broad.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires warranted, trade-expert and sometimes engineer-prepared shop drawings, which edges toward design responsibility.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c174","reasoning_cat1":"Dense and partly garbled, but the allocation — Claims under 4.3.6/4.3.7 and Contractor liability for knowing failures — is stated in specific terms.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 bars claims not embodied in Change Orders, which restricts the Claim route this paragraph presupposes.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c175","reasoning_cat1":"The warranty exclusions ('improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage') and 'may be considered defective' are open-textured, and the transcription is fragmentary.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.5 and A201 12.2 correction obligations run alongside it consistently.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c176","reasoning_cat1":"'Sales, consumer, use and similar taxes' with a timing test tied to bids or negotiations; workable but the 'similar taxes' catch-all is open.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.6.2 makes such taxes a reimbursable Cost of the Work and Exhibit D prescribes a Hawaii excise tax methodology with its own exemptions, so who bears which taxes is set in three places.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c177","reasoning_cat1":"'Customarily secured after execution of the Contract' is a trade-practice test but is conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees reimbursable, and A201 2.2.2 carves permits out of the Owner's obligations, which together are coherent.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c178","reasoning_cat1":"A short compliance obligation.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits with 3.7.3 and 3.7.4 without tension.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c179","reasoning_cat1":"Clear allocation with a notification duty and a Modification route for changes.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent of the Contract Documents and applicable codes at the Contractor's own hand, which pulls against this disclaimer.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c180","reasoning_cat1":"'Appropriate responsibility' is imprecise but the trigger — performing Work knowing it to be contrary to law without notice — is definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.7.3 and with 8.1.6's exclusion of costs from Contractor fault.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c181","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable objection' is the only soft term in an otherwise mechanical allowance rule.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 5.2.4 states no allowances at all, so this machinery has nothing to operate on in this contract.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c182","reasoning_cat1":"A precise three-limb accounting rule for what allowances cover and how Change Orders adjust them.","reasoning_cat2":"It adjusts 'the Contract Sum' while Article 5 frames payment around Cost of the Work plus Fee with a blank GMP, and no allowances were stated in 5.2.4.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c183","reasoning_cat1":"'In sufficient time to avoid delay' is a soft timing standard but a familiar one.","reasoning_cat2":"No allowances are stated in the Agreement, so the obligation is untethered.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c184","reasoning_cat1":"'Competent superintendent and necessary assistants' and the distinction between 'important communications' and other communications are both unmeasured.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum Article 2 requires one designated supervisory employee personally responsible for the project, and 14.4 names a Contractor representative, so three provisions describe site leadership.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c185","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable time to review submittals' is soft but ordinary.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 govern the construction schedule with a different regime, and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds the Owner to every Architect approval.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c186","reasoning_cat1":"'In general accordance with the most recent schedules' is a deliberately loose standard whose enforceability parties dispute.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 3.10.4 makes the Construction Schedule part of the Contract Documents, which is a stronger commitment than 'general accordance'.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c187","reasoning_cat1":"A concrete record-keeping obligation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Agreement Article 11's records requirement and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c188","reasoning_cat1":"A definition with a specific list of document types.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 adds requirements consistent with this definition.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c189","reasoning_cat1":"A short definitional provision, partly illegible in transcription.","reasoning_cat2":"No competing definition appears.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c190","reasoning_cat1":"A definition tied to physical examples and standards.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.12.4 and 4.2.7.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c191","reasoning_cat1":"States clearly that submittals are not Contract Documents and confines their purpose.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 make schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents, so the line between contract and non-contract submittals is drawn differently in different places.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c192","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable promptness' and 'such sequence as to cause no delay' are ordinary construction standards.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.2.7 and Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c193","reasoning_cat1":"A deemed representation with specific content ('determined and verified materials, field measurements and field construction criteria').","reasoning_cat2":"It reinforces Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b)'s verification duty.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c194","reasoning_cat1":"An intricate but carefully conditioned rule about deviations, with two express escape routes.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 permits changes only by Change Order, which narrows limb (1)'s written-approval route.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c195","reasoning_cat1":"A precise notice-and-effect rule for resubmittals.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.12.5 and 4.2.7.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c196","reasoning_cat1":"Long, with several conditional limbs, but each duty and each entitlement to rely is expressly conditioned; the phrase 'unless the Contractor needs to provide such services' is the loosest part.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires licensed engineer preparation 'if required by the Architect or the Owner or applicable law', which may go further than the criteria-specification bargain here.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c197","reasoning_cat1":"'Shall not unreasonably encumber the site' is a soft standard but a minor one.","reasoning_cat2":"No competing site-use provision appears.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c198","reasoning_cat1":"A short and definite responsibility allocation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.14.2 and with the Cost of the Work provisions.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c199","reasoning_cat1":"'Shall not unreasonably withhold' appears on both sides; the drafting is balanced and specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Article 6 separate-contractor provisions.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c200","reasoning_cat1":"Truncated in transcription but the obligation to provide access is simple.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Agreement Article 11's audit and access rights.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c201","reasoning_cat1":"The exception for designs 'required by the Contract Documents' and the 'reason to believe' qualifier are contestable but conventionally drawn.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 7.6.5 expressly deals with royalties as a Cost of the Work and cross-refers to the last sentence of this paragraph, so the two must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c202","reasoning_cat1":"'To the fullest extent permitted by law' and 'only to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions' are carefully bounded, though indemnities of this kind are frequently litigated.","reasoning_cat2":"It is expressed as applying to the extent claims are not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance under Paragraph 11.3, yet Agreement Article 16 states no insurance requirements at all.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c203","reasoning_cat1":"A short anti-limitation rule with a clear referent.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.18.1 and with the workers' compensation coverage evidenced in Exhibit E.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c204","reasoning_cat1":"A definition identifying the Architect by reference to the Agreement.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement names Fung/Howerson as Architect, so the definition has a referent.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c205","reasoning_cat1":"A clear restriction requiring tripartite written consent, with a reasonableness proviso.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 unilaterally adds an Owner consent requirement to every Architect approval, which arguably modifies the Architect's authority without the tripartite consent this paragraph demands.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c206","reasoning_cat1":"Badly garbled in transcription, but the substance — successor Architect subject to no reasonable objection — is standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 14.5 addresses changes of representatives separately and consistently.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"'Will be an Owner's representative' with authority 'only to the extent provided in the Contract Documents' is a familiar but somewhat circular formulation.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 reserves parallel rights to the Owner while disclaiming Owner responsibility, which complicates the Architect's representative role.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.29},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c230","reasoning_cat1":"A short procedural rule with a ten-day response window and three permitted responses.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.4.2 and 4.4.5.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c231","reasoning_cat1":"Calling the decision 'final and binding on the parties but subject to mediation and arbitration' is internally in tension about what finality means.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.4 lets the Contractor demand arbitration of the final accounting 'without a further decision of the Architect', so the Architect's decisional monopoly is qualified elsewhere.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c232","reasoning_cat1":"A conditional preclusion depending on the Architect's decision reciting two specific statements; workable but conditional on the Architect's own drafting.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.4 imposes its own 30-day arbitration deadline running from receipt of the final Certificate, a parallel and differently triggered rule.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c233","reasoning_cat1":"Permissive and short, partly garbled in transcription.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement Article 16 states no bond requirement, so the surety is hypothetical here.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"A short saving provision preserving statutory lien deadlines.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 12.1.4(b) requires lien waivers and Addendum 12.2.2 keys final payment to a lien-free title endorsement, so lien rights are addressed in several places.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c235","reasoning_cat1":"Heavily garbled in transcription; the underlying mediation mechanics (AAA rules, 60-day stay) are standard but hard to read as printed.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.5.3 and 4.6.1's requirement that mediation precede arbitration.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c236","reasoning_cat1":"Equal sharing of fees and a default venue at the Project location; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"No competing venue or cost-allocation provision appears.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c237","reasoning_cat1":"The scope clause carves out 'Claims relating to aesthetic effect' and claims waived under other subparagraphs, and the transcription of those exceptions is fragmentary, leaving the arbitration scope uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.4 provides direct arbitration without an Architect decision, and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 reserves aesthetic control to the Owner, both of which bear on the carve-outs here.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c238","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies the rules and filing requirements specifically.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.6.1 and 4.6.3.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c239","reasoning_cat1":"'Within a reasonable time after the Claim has arisen' sits against fixed cross-referenced deadlines and a statute-of-limitations backstop, mixing three different measures.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.4's 30-day rule adds a fourth limitation period for a particular class of dispute.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"'Substantially involved in a common question of fact or law' and 'whose interest or responsibility is insubstantial' are elastic joinder tests within an otherwise detailed provision.","reasoning_cat2":"Nothing else in the instrument addresses joinder or consolidation.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence enforcement provision.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the rest of Paragraph 4.6.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c242","reasoning_cat1":"A definition with an express exclusion of separate contractors.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Agreement Article 10 and Article 6.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"A short definitional provision.","reasoning_cat2":"No competing definition appears.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"The deeming rule — failure to reply promptly 'shall constitute notice of no reasonable objection' — is definite though 'promptly' is unmeasured.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 10.1 sets a materially different regime in which the Contractor obtains bids and the Owner determines which bids are accepted, and Addendum 6.5 requires at least two bids, so subcontractor selection is governed three ways.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"Two short reciprocal rules turning on 'reasonable and timely objection'.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 10.1's final sentence states the Contractor's side of the same rule, and Agreement 10.2 gives the Owner power to require another bid, which this paragraph does not contemplate.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonably capable of performing' and 'acted promptly and responsively' are judgment standards controlling entitlement to an increase.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 10.2 provides a different remedy for the same situation — a Change Order adjusting the Guaranteed Maximum Price by the bid differential — so two provisions price Owner-forced substitutions differently.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c247","reasoning_cat1":"A single short prohibition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.2.2 and Agreement 10.1's reasonable-objection rule.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c248","reasoning_cat1":"A contingent assignment with three stated conditions; specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 13.3 imposes a duty to execute assignments as a condition of receiving termination payments, which overlaps with this automatic assignment.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"'Equitably adjusted' with a stated suspension threshold; the adjustment measure is open.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 13.4 handles suspension adjustments with its own mapping of 'profit' to the Contractor's Fee.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c250","reasoning_cat1":"A reservation of rights with a claim route cross-referenced to 4.3.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.2 and the Claims provisions.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c251","reasoning_cat1":"A definitional convention for multi-contract projects.","reasoning_cat2":"No separate contracts are identified in this instrument, so the provision is dormant.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c252","reasoning_cat1":"'Deemed necessary after a joint review and mutual agreement' conditions schedule revisions on agreement without a fallback.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 create their own schedule-revision regime that becomes part of the Contract Documents, so schedule authority is stated twice.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c253","reasoning_cat1":"'Including, without excluding others' is an open phrase but the deeming rule is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.1.1 and 6.2.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c254","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable opportunity' is soft but the duty is narrow.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.1.3 and 3.13.1.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c255","reasoning_cat1":"Failure to report is deemed an acknowledgment of fitness 'except as to defects not then reasonably discoverable', an elastic saving clause on a strict deeming rule.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels 3.2.1's study-and-compare duty and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) without contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c256","reasoning_cat1":"'Improperly timed activities' and 'damage to the Work' are undefined but the reciprocal allocation is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"A201 4.3.10's consequential damages waiver limits what can be recovered under this paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c257","reasoning_cat1":"'Wrongfully caused' is undefined and does more work than it appears to.","reasoning_cat2":"Cross-refers consistently to 10.2.5 and to the insurance provisions.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c258","reasoning_cat1":"A single cross-referencing sentence.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.14.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
