{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c289","reasoning_cat1":"A short payment obligation referring out to the Contract Documents for manner and time.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement's 12.1.3 leaves the application cut-off day and the alternative payment period blank, so the time 'provided in the Contract Documents' is incomplete.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c290","reasoning_cat1":"'Promptly pay each Subcontractor ... reflecting percentages actually retained' is specific though the retention reference is external.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.1.8 requires at least ten percent retainage on subcontractor payments while Addendum 12.1.7.3 sets five percent on the Fee, so the retention figures come from more than one place.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c291","reasoning_cat1":"A clear negative covenant with a statutory saving.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1 permits joint payments while disclaiming any obligation to subcontractors, which is consistent.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c292","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.6.2 and Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c293","reasoning_cat1":"A short non-acceptance rule.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.9.3 and 12.2.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c294","reasoning_cat1":"It requires payments to be 'held' for subcontractors while denying that any trust, fiduciary or tort liability arises — a tension built into one sentence.","reasoning_cat2":"It is conditioned on the absence of a payment bond 'in the full penal sum of the Contract Sum', but Article 16 requires no bond and no Contract Sum figure is stated.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c295","reasoning_cat1":"Definite trigger periods (seven days) and a stated remedy of stopping Work plus time and cost recovery.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.1.3's payment dates are blank and Addendum 12.2.2 recasts final payment timing, so the 'date established in the Contract Documents' this remedy depends on is uncertain.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c296","reasoning_cat1":"'Sufficiently complete ... so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use' is the classic evaluative test of substantial completion.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 4.4 pays a bonus for early substantial completion and Addendum 4.3 fixes the target date, so the definition carries money with it.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c297","reasoning_cat1":"A concrete listing obligation with an express non-waiver sentence.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.8.3-9.8.5 and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c298","reasoning_cat1":"An inspection procedure with a defined re-inspection loop.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.8.1 and 9.8.4.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c299","reasoning_cat1":"It fixes the date and allocates responsibilities and warranty commencement 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate', which leaves content to a document not yet drafted.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 requires warranties to be assembled at final payment, and Addendum 4.4's bonus turns on the date established here.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c300","reasoning_cat1":"The obligation to pay retainage is clear, subject to adjustment for incomplete Work.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement's 12.1.7.3 states retainage as 'N/A' while Addendum 12.1.7.3 sets five percent and 12.1.8 sets ten percent for subcontractors, so what retainage is released here is unsettled.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c301","reasoning_cat1":"A short joint-inspection requirement.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.9.3 and 11.4.1.5.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c302","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence non-acceptance rule with an 'unless otherwise agreed' opener.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.6.6.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c303","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed certification standard qualified by 'to the best of the Architect's knowledge, information and belief'.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.3 imposes its own accountants' review and timing and expressly supersedes A201 9.4.1, while Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 adds an Owner acceptance condition to the final Certificate.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c304","reasoning_cat1":"A five-item list closing with 'other data establishing payment or satisfaction of obligations ... to the extent and in such form as may be designated by the Owner', a general catch-all after specifics.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 12.1.4(b) and 12.2.2 add lien-waiver and title-endorsement requirements, and Article 16 specifies no insurance to be certified under item (2).","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c305","reasoning_cat1":"'Materially delayed' governs entitlement, and the comparison to 'retainage stipulated in the Contract Documents' assumes a stipulated figure.","reasoning_cat2":"No consistent retainage figure exists — 12.1.7.3 says 'N/A', the Addendum says five percent, 12.1.8 says ten percent for subcontractors.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c306","reasoning_cat1":"A waiver subject to three enumerated exceptions, which invites an expressio unius argument about anything not listed.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 14.6's representations expressly survive final completion, which sits alongside this waiver and may or may not be covered by the exceptions.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c307","reasoning_cat1":"Waiver on acceptance except for claims 'previously made in writing and identified ... as unsettled' — a precise but easily contested condition.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.2.4's 30-day arbitration rule operates on the same final-payment moment.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c308","reasoning_cat1":"A short, absolute allocation of safety responsibility.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 expressly disclaims Owner responsibility for safety, which reinforces this.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c309","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable precautions' and 'reasonable protection' are the operative measures, but the three protected categories are itemised.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.18 indemnification and the property insurance provisions.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c310","reasoning_cat1":"A compliance obligation in plain terms.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallels 3.7.2 without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},

{"clause_id":"c349","reasoning_cat1":"Three separate accrual rules keyed to Substantial Completion and the final Certificate, and the transcription is badly broken in the third limb, so the deemed accrual dates are hard to read as printed.","reasoning_cat2":"A201 4.6.3 makes the arbitration deadline turn on this paragraph, and 12.2.5 distinguishes the correction period from the limitation period, so the provisions interlock but do not conflict.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c350","reasoning_cat1":"A definite 30-day trigger with four enumerated grounds, though ground .3 depends on payment 'within the time stated in the Contract Documents'.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 12.1.3 leaves the payment dates blank and Addendum 12.2.2 recasts final payment timing, while Agreement 13.1 caps what the Contractor may recover on such a termination.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c351","reasoning_cat1":"The threshold — suspensions constituting 'more than 100 percent of the total number of days scheduled for completion or 120 days in any 365-day period, whichever is less' — is oddly expressed and hard to apply.","reasoning_cat2":"It depends on a schedule for completion that is fixed differently in Agreement 4.3 and Addendum 4.3.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c352","reasoning_cat1":"'Persistently failed to fulfill the Owner's obligations ... with respect to matters important to the progress of the Work' is a doubly evaluative trigger.","reasoning_cat2":"Recovery is by cross-reference to 14.1.3, which Agreement 13.1 caps by reference to the 13.2 calculation, so the remedy is set in two places.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c353","reasoning_cat1":"After three specific grounds the list closes with 'otherwise is guilty of substantial breach of a provision of the Contract Documents', a general catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is exactly the ejusdem generis problem, and 'persistently or repeatedly' is unmeasured.","reasoning_cat2":"Addendum 6.5 gives the Owner a separate right to terminate 'in Owner's sole and absolute discretion' if the Preliminary Budget is unacceptable, a route outside this ostensibly comprehensive termination scheme.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c354","reasoning_cat1":"'Finish the Work by whatever reasonable method the Owner may deem expedient' combines an objective and a subjective standard in one phrase.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 13.2 caps the amount payable on a for-cause termination and A201 5.4.1 governs the subcontract assignment this paragraph invokes.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c355","reasoning_cat1":"The whole calculation turns on 'the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum', a figure the paragraph assumes to be fixed.","reasoning_cat2":"In this cost-plus contract the Contract Sum is Cost of the Work plus Fee with a Guaranteed Maximum Price of 'N/A', and Agreement 13.2 prescribes a different and capped calculation for the same termination, so two incompatible measures apply.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c356","reasoning_cat1":"A broad but plainly stated power to suspend 'for such period of time as the Owner may determine'.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 13.4 supplements it by requiring GMP and Contract Time increases and by redefining 'profit' as the Contractor's Fee, though the GMP is blank.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence conferring an unconditional convenience termination right.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 13.1 caps the payment on such a termination and Addendum 6.5 adds a further discretionary termination right, so the Owner's exit routes are stated in three places.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"Three specific, concrete duties on receipt of notice.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 14.4.1 and with Agreement 13.3's assignment obligations.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"'Reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed' supplies no measure, and 'costs incurred by reason of such termination' is open-ended.","reasoning_cat2":"Agreement 13.1 expressly overrides this by capping the amount at what 13.2 would yield while directing that the Fee be calculated as if the Work had been fully completed, so the two payment rules for the same event differ.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.45}
]}
